observed_effect: The bounded cost check answered its own question only negatively and informatively: cost robustness of the momentum signal is NOT_IDENTIFIED, because the signal has no directional turnover (27/30 cells single-sign; the 3 remaining cells flip on the price level crossing $1). The higher-value information gain is that the admitted 'short-horizon momentum' cell is a constant long position (US large-cap beta) rather than a return-sign bet, which qualifies the entire admitted momentum evidence line and the falsified reversal line that mirrors it, without re-running or overwriting either. The gate stack behaved as designed: independent recomputation reproduced every cell (90/90), the zero-cost column reproduced the published artifact (30/30), and the implausibility of near-zero candidate cost sensitivity was what surfaced the premise defect.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the admitted short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe.
uncertainty_reduced: Reduced on the narrower question actually testable here: the declared cost grid does not identify the cost robustness of a momentum rule on this universe, and the reason is a verified signal-definition defect (mean log price used where a log return is required) that makes the tested series a constant position. New durable evidence: a per-asset/per-lookback weight-composition and turnover audit, plus the observation that the published lookback sweep's medians are identical across lookbacks, which is the signature of a lookback-independent signal. Not reduced: whether short-horizon return autocorrelation exists or survives costs, because no corrected signal was tested; that uncertainty is now explicitly assigned to the next activation rather than left implicit.
research_result: VERIFIED NEGATIVE RESULT with two parts. (1) The cost-robustness question is NOT_IDENTIFIED: the predeclared grid was evaluated and independently reproduced, but the signal under test is a constant long position, so the grid measures the cost sensitivity of a ~3x/year-turnover static exposure (candidate medians essentially unchanged at k=0/1/2: MSFT lb5 [0.052, 0.072], META lb5 [0.073, 0.067, 0.042], TSLA +0.001) while the cost-matched null absorbs full turnover cost. (2) Verified defect: research/backtest/regime_stability.py::momentum_signals (and mean_reversion_signals) use mean log price over the window instead of a log return, so the emitted weight is +1 (resp. -1) at every bar; 27/30 cells are single-sign and the 3 NVDA cells flip only where the price level crosses $1. Consequence: the admitted momentum cell and the falsified reversal cell test constant long/short exposure, not short-horizon return autocorrelation. No prior verdict, figure or history row was altered; the qualification is recorded as an interpretation correction in state/LEARNING_STATE.md.
next: Repair research/backtest/regime_stability.py::momentum_signals to the sign of the previous N-day log return (log(closes[i]/closes[i-lookback])) with a unit test that fails on a single-sign weight series, then re-run the 10-asset momentum cell and the R-001 cost grid on the corrected signal.
